clue.text: Clue I must recast, containing nothing of great precision

indicators.note: to contain is to hold within, so one piece goes inside the other
to recast something is to cast it again in a new form, so the letters are remoulded

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A setter is told to rewrite a clue, and to make the new one exact.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters give METICULUS, and the O for nothing slips in near the end to make METICULOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone meticulous pays careful attention to every small detail, so the word describes exactness and rigour.

clue.text: Online clip and online talks — very skilful

parts.note: a GIF is a short looping image or clip shared online
TED talks are lectures watched online

explanation.surface: Someone praises a creator whose web videos and lectures are brilliantly made.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are internet staples: the GIF image format and the TED talk series.
explanation.definitionFit: A gifted person has natural talent and ability, which matches being highly capable at something.

clue.text: Gala president finally in charge

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: The head of an organisation is placed in control of a gala event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In charge' looks like a phrase meaning responsible, but 'in' is the insertion signal and 'charge' supplies FEE, which takes the T in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor festival or celebration, often held to raise funds, much like a gala.

clue.text: Japan working to secure one ally

definitions.note: a verb here: to ally oneself with

parts.note: J is the international vehicle code for Japan

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A note about Japanese diplomacy: working to gain a partner nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'ally' as a noun, a partner country, but it is a verb meaning to unite with; the I sits inside ON after the J.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally with someone is to unite or combine with them, the same as to join them.

clue.text: Rock musical dance? It's indigestible

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A theatre critic finds a rock show with dancing hard to stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indigestible' looks like a critic's verdict on a show, but it literally describes the clump of hair a cat cannot digest.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairball is a mass of swallowed fur in a cat's stomach that cannot be broken down, so it gets coughed up.

clue.text: African country: cold and hot, notice

parts.note: C for cold, as on a tap
H for hot, as on a tap
an ad, or advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: A traveller's note on a country of extremes: cold nights, hot days, take heed.
explanation.walkthrough: C and H are the letters on cold and hot taps.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked nation in north-central Africa, named after Lake Chad.

clue.text: Someone sent away recalled English Times blocking story

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters run back the other way

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits in the middle of it, so one piece lodges inside another

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A banished person, whose story the Times newspaper suppressed, is called home.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic Times suggests the newspaper, but it is the times sign X. Put X inside LIE, add E in front to get ELIXE, then reverse the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is a person banished from their native land, forced to live abroad.

clue.text: Composer frequently having change of heart, accompanied by different composer

indicators.note: the heart is the middle letter, and changing it swaps that one letter for another

parts.note: often means frequently; its middle T becomes F
Johann Sebastian Bach, a composer other than the one being defined

explanation.surface: A fickle composer keeps changing his mind while working alongside a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of heart' sounds like a mind changed, but it means the central letter of OFTEN is swapped, here T for F, giving OFFEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Offenbach was a nineteenth-century German-French composer of operettas, the theme of this puzzle.

clue.text: Free sea trips enthralling old islanders

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one piece is held inside the other
something that trips stumbles and falls in a muddle, so the letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Complimentary cruises captivate elderly people who live on islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trips' reads as voyages, but it is the anagram signal; 'Free' belongs to the letters, not to the price. The Faeroe Islands lie in the North Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Faeroese are the people of the Faeroe Islands, a self-governing Danish archipelago, so they are islanders.

clue.text: Head of forces in city picked up oblique report

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking something up lifts it so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: the Wen, or Great Wen, is an old name for London, so a wen is a large city in crosswords

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: an oblique is the slash punctuation mark

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A military commander in a city overheard a sly, indirect remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts as overheard, but in a down clue it means lifted, read upwards. 'Oblique' is not indirect: it is another name for the / punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsflash is a brief broadcast bulletin interrupting normal programmes with urgent news, a kind of report.

clue.text: See 17
Later information from university head about degree

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
D is the abbreviation for degree

explanation.surface: A college principal gives fresh news about someone's qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'University head' reads as one person, the principal, but it splits into U and PATE, with D inside PATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An update is the most recent news on a subject, bringing someone current with fresher facts.

clue.text: Peculiar anthem's half-tone off in work by 8

indicators.note: something peculiar is odd or out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, eighteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A musician complains that an odd anthem has a semitone wrong somewhere in a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-tone off' sounds like a musical error, but every letter of it joins the anagram fodder. The 8 refers to the answer at 8 Across, the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tales of Hoffmann is Offenbach's final opera, so it is one of that composer's compositions.

clue.text: See 13
New items turn out to be foods

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: to turn something out is to empty and upend it, leaving the letters jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Fresh products on a menu prove to be edible dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' sits in the fodder, and 'out' with it makes the signal, so only 'items turn' is rearranged after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutriments are nourishing substances, things eaten for sustenance, so the word is a formal synonym.

clue.text: Guess I'm to board large car

indicators.note: to board a vehicle is to get inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: an estate is a British estate car, what Americans call a station wagon
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone guesses they are about to climb into a big vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon, a car with a long rear load space.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to make a rough judgement of a quantity, which is to guess approximately.

clue.text: 8's work revised her opus, beset by criminals?

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange
the criminal world is called the underworld, so being surrounded by criminals is being in it

explanation.surface: A composer reworks a woman's composition and finds himself surrounded by crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: The underworld has two senses: organised crime, which the clue uses, and the realm of the dead, where the mythical Orpheus went to fetch Eurydice. The question mark flags that playful second step.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpheus in the Underworld is Offenbach's 1858 operetta, famous for its galop, so it is a composition by him.

clue.text: Certain South American power getting on top of simple uprising about sport

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece on top of another simply comes first

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps the other
something rising up in a down entry reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: naive means simple or unsophisticated
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A South American power gains the upper hand over an unsophisticated revolt about a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' sounds political, but in a down clue it means the word reads from the bottom up; 'sport' is rugby union, abbreviated in the usual crossword way.
explanation.definitionFit: A Peruvian is a person from Peru, which is one particular country of South America.

clue.text: Fired to eat the whole vegetable

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: shot is a past tense of fire, as a gun
all means the whole

explanation.surface: Someone sacked for eating an entire vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests dismissed from a job, but it is SHOT as from a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small mild onion used in cooking, and onions count as vegetables.

clue.text: Composer starts to record item in small hut

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a cabin is a hut

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so each word gives only its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A composer begins recording a piece in a tiny shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer' at the front is the definition, and the two initial letters slot into the hut word just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Scriabin was a Russian composer and pianist of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

clue.text: Smart greeting is considered pretentious

parts.note: chic means smart and stylish
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A snooty remark that a polished hello comes across as affected.
explanation.walkthrough: Smart and pretentious sit close in meaning, which hides that 'Smart' is wordplay and the definition is at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Chichi describes things that are showily fussy or affectedly elegant, so it means pretentious.

clue.text: Containers from 23 Across?

definitions.note: plural, read as two containers side by side
definitions.meaning: first meaning: two tins, each a can
second meaning: the high-kicking dance featured in that Offenbach operetta

explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'Containers' is read as two cans side by side. The question mark admits the dance is better known from Orpheus in the Underworld, though it also appears in La Vie Parisienne.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a lively high-kicking Parisian dance, closely tied to Offenbach's music, and two tins make a pair of cans.

clue.text: Pensive aria and line arranged from work by 8

indicators.note: to arrange music or anything else is to put it in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, leaving out the joining word 'and'

explanation.surface: A thoughtful song and a vocal line are set from an opera by the theme composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' fits the musical surface neatly but is the anagram signal; 'and' joins the two parts of the fodder without contributing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: La Vie Parisienne is an 1866 operetta by Offenbach, so it is one of that composer's compositions.

clue.text: Idle fellow found under a lot of cargo

indicators.note: in a down entry a piece found under another simply follows it
a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
a load is a cargo

explanation.surface: A lazy man is discovered lying beneath a heap of freight.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the F sits under LOA, the cargo word minus its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf is to spend time idly, lounging around without working, so it means to idle.

clue.text: Nine letters in our alphabet set up one for Greek

indicators.note: in a down entry setting something up raises it so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: the first nine letters of the alphabet run from A to I

explanation.surface: A comparison of alphabets: nine of ours make up a single Greek one.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine letters are described, not listed: their span is written A TO I.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is a letter of the Greek alphabet, the counterpart of our I, so it is one letter for the Greeks.

clue.text: Move slowly, having no leader in an emergency

indicators.note: with no leader nothing comes first, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: a pinch is a crisis or emergency, as in 'at a pinch'

explanation.surface: In a crisis with nobody in charge, everything creeps along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In an emergency' reads as one phrase; 'in' is only the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to creep forward a tiny distance at a time, so it describes moving slowly.

clue.text: A sign that finally consuming meat may be an epiphany

indicators.note: what is consumed goes inside the eater, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: taken as written
ham is a meat
an omen is a sign

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sign that someone at last eating meat could signal a sudden revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: The container is unusual: 'A sign that finally' forms one outer string, and the meat lands right after its opening A rather than in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An aha moment is a sudden flash of insight or understanding, the everyday phrase for that revelation.

clue.text: Trickery caught a large number

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
a raft of things is a large number of them

explanation.surface: Deception has netted a great many victims.
explanation.walkthrough: C for caught comes from cricket scorecards, where it marks a batsman dismissed by a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft in the sense of guile or cunning means skill used to deceive, so it fits trickery.
